pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: KVM: Don't accept obviously wrong gsi values via KVM_IRQFD We cannot add routes for gsi values >= KVM_MAX_IRQ_ROUTES -- see kvm_set_irq_routing(). Hence, there is no sense in accepting them via KVM_IRQFD. Prevent them from entering the system in the first place. BUG=chromium:770154 TEST=Build and run Change-Id: Idcc9f7606d1238645bbb4fd2def264a9f9f7071f Signed-off-by: Jan H. Schnherr <jschoenh@amazon.de> Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 36ae3c0a36b) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/692736 Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: KVM: VMX: Do not BUG() on out-of-bounds guest IRQ The value of the guest_irq argument to vmx_update_pi_irte() is ultimately coming from a KVM_IRQFD API call. Do not BUG() in vmx_update_pi_irte() if the value is out-of bounds. (Especially, since KVM as a whole seems to hang after that.) Instead, print a message only once if we find that we don't have a route for a certain IRQ (which can be out-of-bounds or within the array). This fixes CVE-2017-1000252. UPSTREAM: kvm: nVMX: Don't allow L2 to access the hardware CR8 If L1 does not specify the "use TPR shadow" VM-execution control in vmcs12, then L0 must specify the "CR8-load exiting" and "CR8-store exiting" VM-execution controls in vmcs02. Failure to do so will give the L2 VM unrestricted read/write access to the hardware CR8. This fixes CVE-2017-12154. Usage: rma_reset --key_id <arg> --board_id <arg> --device_id <arg> --hw_id <arg> | --auth_code <arg> These value are used for generating the challenge response and all are mandatory. -k,--key_id Index of the server private key -b,--board_id BoardID type field -d,--device_id Device-unique identifier -w,--hw_id Hardware id The -t parameter, not listed, will use the default values to generate the challenge response This value is the authorization code and any other parameters are ignored -a,--auth_code Reset authorization code BUG=b:37952913 BRANCH=none TEST=make buildall Signed-off-by: Sam Hurst <shurst@chromium.org> Change-Id: Idc916b123928328a3425fa4eee22afc2ec179fc1 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/665388 Commit-Ready: Sam Hurst <shurst@google.com> Commit-Ready: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sam Hurst <shurst@google.com> Reviewed-by: Michael Tang <ntang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: platform/x86: intel_pmc_core: Add PMC wake source detection The patch adds support to detect the source of wake from suspend-to-ram and suspend-to-idle state for Intel Sunrise Point PCH based platforms. This is intended to be used for diagnosing spurious wake ups during stability testing. The patch decodes the wake source from Power Management Controller (PMC) registers PM1_EN_STS and GPE0_STS. Supported wake sources: From PM1_EN_STS - Power Button, RTC, PCI Express Wake From GPE0_STS - Hot Plug, Software GPE, TCO SCI, SMBus Wake, PCI Express, Battery Low, PME, PME Bus 0, GPIO Tier2, LAN_WAKE#, WADT, and generic GPE events GPE_STS[95:0] Sample output from debugfs below: Example #1 - cat /sys/kernel/debug/pmc_core/sleep_wake_source Wake Source: RTC Example #2 - cat /sys/kernel/debug/pmc_core/sleep_wake_source Wake Source: PME Bus 0 BUG=b:37219929 TEST=Put device in sleep state, then wake up using power button, RTC, USB keyboard etc. Read the wake source from debugfs. Change-Id: Ie72227febe462248a57cf40a7e59c4f60fbcc68d Signed-off-by: Rushikesh S Kadam <rushikesh.s.kadam@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/641092 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org>

chrome_cr50: change version regexp Change the version regular expression, so it will match the entire line. We expect that \d+ will match all of the digits that are after '.', but we dont necessarily get all of the characters on a line at once. We may only get the first digit from servo. This is good enough to match, the expression, but not what we actually want. We sometimes got '0.0.2' instead of '0.0.27'. This changes the expression to require it to match a whitespace character at the end of the version. This way we know we got the entire version string. Now there are still the occational console command timeouts, but we no longer get a cutoff version. BUG=b:66211730 BRANCH=none TEST=read cr50.get_version() a bunch. Count the number of times it drops the last character of the version. Verify it is now 0. Change-Id: Ie9fdfb104df946f1b65dc7c0c18e320476b28a6a Signed-off-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/687968 Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>
